## Benchmarks for self-improvement, RSI and continual agents

*Scope: benchmarks, gyms and evaluation protocols that score (a) agents improving their own harness, memory or skills on a frozen model, (b) agents doing the AI R&D steps that would feed recursion (data, training, compression, infrastructure), (c) systems whose updated version runs the next round (true recursion), and (d) continual and lifelong streams with drift. Coverage is about 60 papers, Jun–18 Nov 2026, plus ICLR 2027 submissions. Read in full this session (✓): RSI-Env, SelfImprove-Bench, Continual AutoResearch, HarnessOpt-Bench, Flex-RSI, Are Self-Evolving Agents Continual Learners?, SEAGym (method and results), Evo-Bench (method and results), Singularity-Bench (§1–5), and RSIBench-Data (abstract, results table, limitations). Partially read (✓ only for the sections cited): GDPevo, EvoHarnessBench, EvoAgentBench, CompressionBench, RSIGym, Auditing-the-Product, AI4AI-Bench (abstract and §1 in full text), CL-Bench, CLE (abstract and main results table). The survey framings come from the four survey digests: Duan 2609.11873, Chen 2607.07663, Ren 2607.13104 and Dai/Ruan "Experience→Structure". I re-read their evaluation sections (✓ Duan §3.5–3.6 and Table 8; Ren §8; Chen §9 item 6). A second adversarial fact-check pass re-opened these full texts; see the log at the end.*

### At a glance
- **What this corner is.** Since June 2026 at least 40 benchmarks or gyms claim to measure "self-improvement", "RSI" or "continual learning" for LLM agents. They fall into four families: harness/experience-evolution benchmarks (frozen model), AI-R&D benchmarks (an agent improves a model, data, a compression scheme or a system), open-ended recursive environments (the updated system runs the next round), and continual/drift streams.
- **State of the art (numbers):**
  - Evo-Bench: best evolver +16.6 overall, still below the human harness (46.3 vs 47.5) ✓.
  - HarnessOpt-Bench: best optimizer captures about ⅔ of OfficeQA headroom ✓.
  - RSIGym: Opus 5 RSI-Index 0.4809, on dev-seen tasks ✓.
  - Singularity-Bench: Opus 5.5 + Claude Code Singularity-Index 1.25 vs human baselines; the other 10 agents average 0.60 ✓.
  - AI4AI-Bench: best 0.250, where 0.1 is the shipped algorithm and 1.0 the optimum ✓.
  - CLE: best system (Claude Code / Opus 5) clears 47.7% of levels ✓.
- **Consensus 1: endpoint gain overstates improvement.**
  - Visible validation scores are optimistic (HarnessOpt-Bench) ✓.
  - Among searches that continue past their best score, 78.26% of RSIBench-Data searches end lower ✓.
  - SEAGym's AHE run collapses to 6/80 replay mid-run and then recovers ✓.
  - Trace Evolution Bench shows a frozen `no_evolve` rescore moving 5–12.5 pp across seeds ◐.
- **Consensus 2: gains are local and do not reliably transfer.**
  - SelfImprove-Bench: replay (G0) falls below the historical score in 8 of 18 method–task pairs, and rankings reverse at G2 ✓.
  - SEAGym: cross-backend out-of-distribution (OOD) gains are mostly neutral or negative ✓.
  - Continual learners: plasticity–stability r = −0.72 (n = 12) ✓.
  - EvoHarnessBench: the harness growing alone causes forgetting of up to −34.7% backward transfer ✓.
- **Consensus 3: persistence buys speed, not final quality** (Continual AutoResearch ✓; CL-Bench, where naive in-context learning beats dedicated memory systems ◐).
- **Consensus 4: the base model matters more than the mechanism.**
  - HarnessOpt-Bench: swapping the optimizer model moves gain about 1.8× more than swapping the coding harness ✓.
  - GDPevo: "magnitude of evolution comes mainly from the model's intelligence" ✓.
- **Biggest open problem.** Nearly every benchmark scores the *product* (the final agent or model). None scores the *process*, that is, whether a later improver beats an earlier one from the same start at matched budget (the "swap test"). Auditing-the-Product finds only 4 of 26 improver claims have such a comparison ✓. The new benchmarks also run almost everything once, with no seeds.

### How it developed

| Month (2026) | Paper | What changed |
|---|---|---|
| Jun | CL-Bench 2606.05661; AgentCL 2606.02461 | Expert-validated continual-learning streams with a "gain over stateless" metric. Naive ICL is a strong baseline ◐ |
| Jun | SEAGym 2606.17546 | First harness-evolution *environment*: train / update-validation / ID / OOD / replay / cost views, wrapping Harbor tasks ✓ |
| Jul | EvoAgentBench 2607.05202 | Train/test linked by an Ability Graph. Curated Ability content transfers; no automatic method is positive everywhere ✓ |
| Jul | RSIBench-Data 2607.25886 | Agent as data-centric researcher on a fixed Tinker stack. Names the "discovery–reliability gap" ✓ |
| Aug | GDPevo 2608.03764; PAST-Bench 2608.04003 | Rule hybridization makes train→test gains attributable. Persistence on/off ablation plus mechanism-evidence score ✓/◐ |
| Aug | HarnessOpt-Bench 2608.06301; Evo-Bench 2608.09096 | Harness optimization becomes a *scored capability*: trusted evaluator, hidden test split, resolution bands, release ladders ✓ |
| Aug | AI4AI-Bench 2608.20318; PACE-Bench 2608.14441; S3Gym 2608.31100 | Training-algorithm design as RSI. Re-adaptation after physics shift. Self-judging accuracy does not predict gain ✓/◐ |
| Sep | EvoHarnessBench 2609.04280; EvoPathBench 2609.24663; SEABench 2609.35596 | Drift moves *into the harness*. Process-level checkpoints. Endogenous misalignment ✓/◐ |

Lifelong ARC streams. A training set to *improve* model-training ability ✓/◐ |

### Taxonomy

The survey framings give three cuts:

- **Duan et al. 2609.11873** classify RSI by autonomy level, L1–L5 (execution → strategy → experience → deployment → recursive). Their Table 8 lists what an L5 evaluation must measure: adaptivity, retention, transfer, efficiency, stability, plus "meta-recursion" (mechanism reuse, successor quality, goal and stopping decisions). They add that these are "proposed requirements… rather than capabilities established by existing RSI benchmarks" ✓.
- **Ren et al. 2607.13104** split by update channel: foundation-model weights θ vs scaffold Σ. They also split evaluation interface (single-shot vs interactive) and separate *mechanism* benchmarks from *domain* benchmarks (§8.2) ✓.
- **Chen et al. 2607.07663** flag that "recognizing frame revision… has neither a benchmark nor a measurement convention" (§9 item 6) ✓.
- **Dai/Ruan ("Experience→Structure")** propose controlled, longitudinal tests of whether "inherited state help[s] produce more effective future updates under comparable… budgets" ✓.

The benchmarks themselves map onto these cuts as follows.

| Family (what is improved / what is measured) | Duan level | Representative benchmarks |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Harness/experience evolution on a frozen model: endpoint and held-out gain** | L2–L3 | Evo-Bench, HarnessOpt-Bench, HarnessDev, GDPevo, EvoAgentBench, EvoCowork, FinEvo-Bench, SkillFlow, Do-Skills-Generalize 2609.39148 |
| **B. Generalization ladders and process/trajectory views** | L3 (Table 8 rows 1–5) | SelfImprove-Bench (G0–G4), SEAGym (replay, ID/OOD, cost), EvoPathBench, Trace Evolution Bench (seed-null), PAST-Bench (mechanism evidence), Beneath the Surface 2611.07624 |
| **C. Continual / drift streams (plasticity, stability, forgetting)** | L3–L4 | Continual learners 2610.25858, EvoHarnessBench, CL-Bench, CLE, AgentCL, Continual-ARC, ServeLearnBench, ReScopeBench, PACE-Bench, Δτ-Bench, SkillShift-Bench, Coding-Agents-Continual 2611.03219, EmbodiedCLBench |
| **D. AI-R&D single-shot (agent improves a model or system; no inheritance)** | L1–L2 | Singularity-Bench, AI4AI-Bench, RSIBench-Data, RSIBench-Code, CompressionBench, Infrathon, Auto-Research Arena, EvalResearchBench, PostTrainBench-family, RSI-Index (Vals) |
| **E. Multi-session / multi-round AI-R&D with inherited state** | L2–L3 | RSIGym, VibeTraining-Bench, ParetoRSI-Gym, RSI-Forge (3 sessions), RSI Arena (2 stages), Continual AutoResearch |
| **F. Recursion proper: the updated system or improver runs the next round** | L5 (partial) | RSI-Env (Self vs Teacher), Flex-RSI (improver edits itself; frozen vs self pairs; hand-offs), SelfImprove-Bench HyperDSH fixed-improver ablation |
| **G. Meta-evaluation and verification of claims** | L5 "meta-recursion" | Auditing-the-Product 2610.27610, "Why is RSI hard to verify?" (ICLR27 OnzWTehIaN), RSI Tax 2611.13524, HDA 2610.22466 |
| **H. Safety and hacking under self-improvement** | cross-cutting | Singularity-Bench red-teaming / Breakwater, RSI-Forge shortcut codebook, SEABench, CheatBench, Masked Erosion |
| **I. Training data to improve the improver** | — | RSI-Dojo 2611.03698, RSI-Prime 2611.23138 |

### Paper cards

**Auditing the Product, Not the Recursion** ([2610.27610](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27610), 2026-10-20, preprint)
- *What it does:* a meta-research census of the evidence behind RSI claims, with a claim-indexed reporting standard.
- *Setup:*
  - Full-text coding of 114 studies, 90 self-described RSI, in an arXiv frame frozen October 2026 ✓ (abstract; §1).
  - Independent human coding, third-reader adjudication, and blind coding of improver comparisons.
- *Key results:*
  - Among the 90 RSI studies:
    - 60% evaluate on tasks not used for selection ✓;
    - 22% audit two or more reruns ✓.
    - In a human-coded random sample the figures are lower still: 45% and 14% ✓ (abstract).
  - Of 26 studies claiming a better improver, 23 report a related comparison but only 4 compare earlier vs later procedures from identical starts at matched budget ✓.
  - Proposition 3 ("diagonal non-identification", §4.3): improver gain is identified only with off-diagonal observations, i.e. a swap test ✓.
- *Limitations / critiques:*
  - It runs no swap test itself.
  - Its frame predates most of the November benchmarks.
  - The ICLR27 submission "Why Is RSI Hard to Verify?" (OnzWTehIaN) gives a complementary finite-horizon sufficiency criterion and statistical tests ◐.

**SelfImprove-Bench: Evaluating Generalization in Self-Improving Agents** ([2611.02797](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.02797), 2026-11-02, preprint; SJTU/Theseus Labs, the same group as the Duan survey)
- *What it does:* procedurally generated game tasks (templates × difficulty × seed) with a five-level generalization ladder:
  - G0 replay;
  - G1 new instances;
  - G2 harder;
  - G3 another game, same capability;
  - G4 cross-capability.

  It is scored by the Headroom-Closed Index (HCI) and adds LLM-annotated trace analysis.
- *Setup:*
  - Methods: ACE (experience), AHE (harness), HyperAgents (meta).
  - Six games (Farm, Combat, Sweepmine, Hero, MC, Astray).
  - Backbones: GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5, DeepSeek-v4.1-flash, with Codex or DeepSeek Harness.
  - No seeds reported.
- *Key results:*
  - G0 replay is below the historical score in 8 of 18 method–task pairs ✓ (§4, "(G0) Retention").
  - G1 is positive in 16 of 18 ✓.
  - G2 reverses rankings: on Farm, HyperAgents beats AHE at training difficulty but trails it on Hard ✓.
  - HyperAgents' G3 transfer from Combat→Farm (109.2% HCI) exceeds direct refinement (100%) ✓.
  - G4 is positive in 5 of 8 directions ✓.
  - Across 915 retained "opinions":
    - 87.9% target prompt/memory, 12.1% the execution harness, and none modify the improver ✓;
    - HyperAgents' revision rate is 40.2% vs ACE 14.2% (AHE 30.6%) ✓.
  - Fixed-improver HyperDSH scores 1.207 vs 1.326 editable, both on DeepSeek, single game ✓.
  - Task scheduling (HyperAgents, Table 4): random medium-difficulty training beats fixed-instance training on Combat (Medium 1.433 vs 0.772; Hard 1.314 vs 0.507). On Hard Combat, mixed and increasing-difficulty curricula score 1.195 and 1.080, also below random medium ✓. *(Corrected: the draft compared 1.433 against 1.080, but 1.433 is a Medium-Combat score and 1.080 a Hard-Combat score. On Medium Hero, fixed-instance training is actually higher, 0.100 vs 0.085.)*
- *Limitations / critiques:*
  - Games only and single instances.
  - The unit is LLM-extracted "opinions", not edits.
  - System and edit surface are confounded across methods (round-3 critique).
  - Improver comparisons are not same-start or matched-budget.

**Flex-RSI: Benchmarking Recursive Self-Improvement of Frontier Agents** ([2611.08946](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08946), 2026-11-06, technical report, TAMU + 12 institutions)
- *What it does:* each round, an executor edits the solution, which is kept only if held-out validation rises. An improver then edits the harness, *including itself*. The final solution is scored on hidden test data.
- *Setup:*
  - 24 tasks in six areas (perception, reasoning, robot action, 3D reconstruction, visual creation, infrastructure); 18 models (11 closed) ✓.
  - Every run starts from the same general harness.
  - Median 49.7M tokens per run ✓.
- *Key results:*
  - On "builds-the-solution" tasks with scaled feedback, models start 0.9 points apart and end 38.8 apart ✓.
  - On the four success/fail-only tasks (RoboCasa, LIBERO-MAX, LIBERO-PRO, ARC-AGI-3), the median open-weight gain is 1.6 vs 16.9 for closed models ✓.
  - Token use vs score has rank correlation −0.05 ✓.
  - Frozen vs self-improving harness: the self-improving run is better in 6 of 7 pairs, by +2.0 to +40.0 ✓. However, the frozen runs ended after fewer rounds in 6 of 7 pairs ✓.
  - A harness handed from a stronger model helped a weaker one in only 2 of 4 tasks (+20.0 Open Drawer, +1.4 3D Tracking) ✓.
- *Limitations / critiques:*
  - Every cell is n = 1.
  - Paired runs are not compute-matched.
  - There is no self-edit rate and no weight updates.
  - A 400-line cap applies to improver self-edits ✓ (FULLTEXT_VERIFICATION).

**RSI-Env: An Open-Ended Environment for Recursive Self-Improvement of Agents** ([2611.01736](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01736), 2026-11-01, ICLR27 submission PwLSweAzxz)
- *What it does:* a persistent sandbox in which the improver can train weights (Tinker SFT/RL) and edit the harness. A host controller holds evaluation and versioning. Under **Self**, each accepted model–harness version runs the next round. Under **Teacher**, a fixed Codex (GPT-5.6 Sol or GPT-6 Astra) does.
- *Setup:*
  - Start: Qwen3.8-27B with a minimal loop.
  - Three settings: Open-General, Capability-Directed (Reasoning, Agentic, Knowledge), Benchmark-Guided.
  - Budget: 10 rounds × 3 h (30 h per run) ✓.
  - Evaluation: GPQA-D (198), AIME 2026 (30), Terminal-Bench 2.1 (89), SimpleQA (500 subset), avg@3 or pass@3 ✓.
- *Key results:*
  - Open-General Self: GPQA 65.2→73.2, AIME 53.3→56.7, via a harness-only update (H1/M0) ✓.
  - Knowledge Self: 82.0→85.0 (harness) →88.0 (after training on 48 self-made SFT pairs) ✓. This is the only two-step harness→weights recursion the paper walks through and that improves its target. Reasoning Self also ended at H1/M1, but its target gain was modest (GPQA +4.0, AIME 0.0) ✓. *(Corrected: the draft called Knowledge the "only" such case without mentioning Reasoning Self's accepted model update.)*
  - Gains come with regressions: Knowledge Self's GPQA falls to 53.0 ✓.
  - Teachers are not consistently better, but they used only 1.19–6.97 h of the 30 h vs 24.9–28.95 h for Self, and never accepted a model update (all M0) ✓.
- *Limitations / critiques:*
  - Apparently one run per cell.
  - AIME has n = 30.
  - Acceptance is validity-only, so there is no gate on capability.
  - The Self-vs-Teacher contrast is confounded by budget use.
  - It is "recursion" in the Duan *structural* sense, not shown to be *effective*.

**Are Self-Evolving Agents Continual Learners?** ([2610.25858](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25858), 2026-10-19, Mila/GDM)
- *What it does:* four drift streams built from BIRD, BFCL and ScienceWorld:
  - topic drift;
  - workflow drift (BFCL-Miss vs BFCL-Base require opposite behaviours);
  - domain drift;
  - compound drift.

  Performance is decomposed into plasticity P and stability S = −(interference + forgetting).
- *Setup:*
  - ReasoningBank, GEPA, Meta-Harness on Gemini 3.6 Flash.
  - Blocks of 50 tasks, 8 rollouts per evaluation instance, binary feedback.
- *Key results:*
  - Overall terminal advantage: GEPA +3.7, ReasoningBank +2.5, Meta-Harness +1.4 pp ✓.
  - GEPA has the most plasticity (+6.2) and least stability (−4.3) ✓.
  - The P–S trade-off has r = −0.72 (p = 0.008, n = 12) ✓.
  - Meta-Harness looks stable only because its gate rejects half or more of candidates. Without the gate, S falls to −3.1 on topic drift and −5.5 on workflow drift ✓.
  - GEPA compresses the BIRD sections from 3,386 to 1,034 characters, erasing a +4.0 gain ✓.
  - Interleaving the stream does not fix it ✓.
- *Limitations / critiques:*
  - One model.
  - Edit surface is confounded with method.
  - Drift is semi-synthetic.

**From AutoResearch to Continual AutoResearch** ([2611.05108](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05108), 2026-11-03, ICLR27 OPHp9Aei9U; RBC Borealis)
- *What it does:* persistent vs reset instances of the same command-line agent on matched ordered streams (9 task families). Metrics are outcome, initialization and time-convergence gain, all on hidden test scores.
- *Setup:*
  - Agents: Sonnet 4.6, Opus 5, GPT-5.4, GPT-5.6-Sol, Kimi K3.
  - 30-min tasks, 32 transfer tasks per agent.
  - Single matched pair per configuration; the GPT-5.6-Sol repeat varied ≤ 0.75 points on outcome and initialization gains ✓.
- *Key results:*
  - Time-convergence gain is positive for all five agents (+3.0 to +21.3) ✓.
  - The stateful lead shrinks from +24.0 at 25% of budget to +1.2 at the deadline ✓.
  - Outcome gain is −0.9 to +7.6, and only Sonnet's is substantial ✓.
  - Subtracting the first-valid reward makes every gain negative ✓.
  - Matched vs shuffled insight cards show small or negative effects on outcome ✓.
  - The agents with the highest reset outcome (Opus 5, GPT-5.6-Sol) show the smallest gains on outcome and initialization. This is our reading of Table 2, not a claim the paper makes, and GPT-5.4 (lower baseline, small gains) breaks the pattern ◐. *(Corrected: the draft's "Stronger models gain less ✓" stated as a paper finding.)*
- *Limitations / critiques:*
  - Streams are only 3–5 tasks long.
  - The CLI scaffold is confounded with model.
  - Self-diagnosed: the memory ablation covers one stream only.

**SEAGym: An Evaluation Environment for Self-Evolving LLM Agents** ([2606.17546](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17546), 2026-06-16, Tsinghua)
- *What it does:* turns Harbor benchmarks into epoch/batch evolution sources with update-validation, ID, OOD, replay and cost views.
- *Setup:*
  - ACE, TF-GRPO, AHE on DeepSeek-V4-Flash.
  - 80 TB2.0+HLE training tasks / 35 validation / 55 test / 80 OOD.
  - 5 epochs, batch size 20.
- *Key results:*
  - AHE is the only method positive on validation (+17.1), ID (+9.1) and OOD (+6.3) ✓ (ACE is also positive on all three but small: +2.9/+3.6/+2.5).
  - TF-GRPO: validation +17.1 but OOD −2.5 ✓.
  - AHE replay: 34→43/80 overall, but 6/80 after epoch 4; 13 tasks fixed, 4 forgotten ✓.
  - Batch size is non-monotone: batch 20 gains most (+17.1 validation), batch 40 gains little (+2.9), and batches 10 and 80 lose 14–17 pp ✓ (Table 3). *(Corrected: the draft said "only batch 20 gains".)*
  - An HLE-only source collapses to 0 at the final snapshot ✓ (Table 4).
  - Cross-backend transfer is asymmetric: a GPT-5.4-evolved harness gives GPT-5.4 ID +5.5 but OOD −7.5 ✓.
- *Limitations / critiques:*
  - Single runs.
  - Harness-only.
  - Two source benchmarks.

*Note on AHE's "only method positive":* in Table 2, ACE's deltas are all positive too (+2.9 validation, +3.6 ID, +2.5 OOD). The paper's point is that only AHE gains substantially on all three. I kept the draft's wording with that caveat.

**HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization** ([2608.06301](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06301), 2026-08-06, Scale AI)
- *What it does:* an optimizer (LLM plus coding harness) edits a pinned seed harness under an evaluation budget (cases and calls) and nominates a candidate. The candidate is scored on a hidden test split as normalized gain, with per-task "resolution bands".
- *Setup:*
  - 5 optimizer models × {opencode, native harness} × 4 tasks (OfficeQA, BrowseComp-Plus, Terminal-Bench, GAIA stub).
  - 111 scored runs, each configuration run twice.
- *Key results:*
  - Model effect 0.142 vs harness effect 0.079, about 1.8× ✓.
  - Across 5 GPT releases on OfficeQA, gain rises monotonically 0.03→0.49 ✓.
  - Lever-coverage breadth vs gain has ρ +0.34 to +0.88 ✓.
  - Share of actions spent reading traces vs gain has ρ −0.31 to −0.64; detailed traces were requested only 16 times (by 7 of 111 cells) ✓.
  - Case passes bind: the median optimizer uses 82% of its case allowance (but only 4% of calls) ✓.
  - The best validation score is optimistic relative to test ✓.
  - Native harness wins only 9 of 20 pairs ✓.
- *Limitations / critiques:*
  - Self-described as "hack-resistant, not hackproof" ✓.
  - One pinned target model per task.
  - Seed complexity is not varied.
  - Breadth is an *outcome*, not a randomized treatment (round-3 critique).

**Evo-Bench: Can Language Models Improve Agent Harness?** ([2608.09096](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09096), 2026-08-10, RUC/BOSS Zhipin)
- *What it does:* tasks are pre-selected for harness sensitivity using 12 auxiliary evolved harnesses (K = 12) ✓, then split by stratum. An evolver improves a CodeAct seed for a fixed DeepSeek-V4-Flash policy.
- *Setup:*
  - 9 evolvers.
  - Budget: 20 iterations / 1,000 steps / 48 h.
  - Single runs ("We run all experiments one time") ✓.
- *Key results:*
  - GPT-5.6 Sol 46.3 overall (+16.6), Opus 4.8 45.8 (+16.1), vs human composite 47.5 ✓.
  - Search +32.8, Office about +0–3 ✓.
  - Early saturation; most models stop before the budget ✓.
  - GPT-5.6 Sol costs over $500 per run, while GLM-5.2 and Qwen3.7-Max reach the knee for under $40 ✓.
- *Limitations / critiques:*
  - Sensitivity-based task selection biases the benchmark toward tasks where harnesses matter, which inflates apparent evolvability.
  - Its claim that harnesses are "highly transferable" across policies ✓ contrasts with SEAGym's asymmetric transfer.

**Singularity-Bench: Can Agents Build Agents?** ([2611.16591](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16591), v2 2026-11-16, ICLR27 hrNam06fy0; CMU/Infini-AI)
- *What it does:* six end-to-end tasks, each against a production human baseline on identical GB300 hardware (12 h on one 4× GB300 node per task ✓):
  - pre-training (vs OLMo-2 recipe);
  - mid-training for RL (vs PRISM);
  - multi-turn RL for a SWE agent (vs Miles);
  - FP8 serving of GLM-5.3-Flash (vs SGLang);
  - a coding harness (vs Claude Code);
  - serverless cluster orchestration (vs Dynamo).

  The Singularity-Index is the mean ratio to human, with failures counted as 0.
- *Setup:*
  - 11 agents (7 models × Codex/Claude Code).
  - About 4,000 GB300-h in total, about 350 per agent ✓.
- *Key results:*
  - Opus 5.5 + CC: index 1.251 at $425 API spend; it beats the baseline on five tasks and matches Miles on post-training (0.533 vs 0.539) ✓.
  - GPT-6.1 Sol + Codex: 0.968 ✓.
  - The other 10 agents average 0.60; proprietary agents average 1.01 and open-weight agents 0.53 ✓.
  - Harness choice swings a model's index (GLM 5.3: 0.656 with CC vs 0.373 with Codex) ✓.
  - Plain Harbor graders were beaten by red-team attacks spanning 9 of 10 OWASP agentic categories. Breakwater catches every attack tested, and one real incident occurred in an informal run (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, coding-harness task) ✓.
- *Limitations / critiques:*
  - Single-shot: nothing is inherited, so it measures L1–L2 capability, not recursion. The "may have the skills needed to reach the singularity" framing ✓ conflates the two (cf. Auditing-the-Product's product/process distinction).
  - Human baselines are fixed recipes, not tuned under the same 12 h.
  - The aggregate index mixes incommensurable ratios.

**RSIBench-Data** ([2607.25886](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25886), 2026-07-28, ICLR27 yeZb6GEcaO; Evolvent/NUS)
- *What it does:* agents iteratively design training data for LoRA-SFT of Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base on a fixed Tinker stack. Evaluation runs on Harbor/E2B.
- *Setup:*
  - 4 researcher agents (Claude Code Opus-4.8/Sonnet-5; Codex gpt-5.6-sol/terra).
  - 6 benchmarks.
  - One representative run per setting ✓.
- *Key results:*
  - The agent improves on its first valid attempt in 58.33% of settings ✓.
  - Of searches that continue past their best score, 78.26% end lower ✓.
  - No agent dominates across benchmarks ✓.
- *Limitations / critiques:* checkpoint selection and official evaluation share the same subset, so the scores are "not generalization to statistically held-out tasks" (authors) ✓.

**GDPevo** ([2608.03764](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03764), 2026-08-04, ICLR27 NOapw3FRkO; PrismShadow/NYU)
- *What it does:* rule hybridization. Enterprise workflows are split into atomic rules, distributed over training tasks and recombined in test tasks, so that gains are attributable. Regeneration counters contamination.
- *Setup:*
  - 120 tasks, 12 groups (5 train + 5 test each) ✓.
  - 4 agents × {base, fewshot, reflect, self} supervision.
- *Key results:*
  - Every evolved combination beats base, by +2.59 to +16.44 pp ✓.
  - Oracle ceiling is 91.6% ✓.
  - Opus 4.8 has the highest base and the largest gain ✓.
  - Fewshot overfits the source group; reflect transfers better ✓.
  - Opus 4.8's amortized cost rises from $1.37 to $1.87 per task ✓.
- *Limitations / critiques:*
  - Synthetic rule worlds.
  - Five test tasks per group.

**EvoHarnessBench** ([2609.04280](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04280), 2026-09-03, ICLR27 tNNCBiSaC9; Salesforce)
- *What it does:* puts non-stationarity in the supplied harness: tools, skills and agents arrive in stages. 17 streams (3–6 stages each), 802 tasks ✓.
- *Key results:*
  - Expansion alone causes forgetting: −12.1% (tools), −13.8% (skills), −46.4% (agents) in the headline figure ✓.
  - Max backward-transfer forgetting is −34.7% for agent-pool expansion ✓.
  - Best adaptation gains: +27.8% (MemToolAgent), +27.5% (GEPA), +110.2% (Meta-Harness on agents) ✓.
- *Limitations / critiques:* deterministic, constructed streams.

**AI4AI-Bench** ([2608.20318](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20318), 2026-08-20, ICLR27 alNtyGHCG3)
- *What it does:* 10 frozen research repositories. The agent rewrites the training algorithm (4 h on one B300), which is rerun from scratch for up to 12 h ✓.
- *Key results:*
  - Across 29 configurations of 6 systems: mean score 0.166, best 0.250, where 0.1 is the shipped algorithm and 1.0 the optimum ✓.
  - Submissions that change how the model learns score 0.226 vs 0.126 ✓.
  - More reasoning effort raises that share from 8% to 64% of submissions, and the mean score from 0.094 to 0.196 ✓.
- *Limitations / critiques:* only the abstract and §1 were read (now in full text); per-task tables are unread.

**CompressionBench** ([2611.06858](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.06858), v2 2026-11-09, CMU)
- *What it does:* the agent builds compressed weights plus inference code under a storage limit.
- *Key results:*
  - 29 of 36 submissions pass verification ✓.
  - The best design per task averages +3.4% perplexity over BF16 and 77.33% vs 79.56% downstream accuracy ✓.
  - Complete-model feedback reverses 17 of 79 local rankings ✓.
  - One run per agent–task pair ✓.

### Consensus, debates & contradictions
- **Consensus: the endpoint is not the process.**
  - Process diagnostics are now standard: SEAGym's multi-view records (update-validation, ID, OOD, replay, cost), SelfImprove-Bench's ladder, EvoPathBench checkpoints, TEB seed bands. *(Corrected: the draft said "SEAGym's Table 8 dimensions"; Table 8 belongs to the Duan survey.)*
  - The Duan survey's L5 table (Table 8) is effectively the field's checklist ✓.
  - Ren §8.1 adds "regression rates on previously solved instances" and a full cost breakdown as required reporting ✓.
- **Consensus: selection, not generation, is the bottleneck.** The evidence:
  - 78.26% of RSIBench-Data searches that continue past their peak end below it;
  - HarnessOpt's optimistic validation;
  - RSIGym's dev-seen scores;
  - Continual AutoResearch's selection-regret analysis;
  - Evo-Bench's early peak, then "detrimental modifications".
- **Debate: do stronger models make better improvers?**
  - Yes: HarnessOpt (monotone GPT ladder ✓), GDPevo ✓, Flex-RSI (closed ≫ open on binary feedback ✓), Singularity-Bench ✓.
  - Not consistently: RSI-Env ("stronger models are not consistently better improvers"; Teachers ≤ Self, but confounded by Teachers using ≤ 7 of 30 h ✓). Continual AutoResearch hints at the same thing: the highest-baseline agents show the smallest persistence gains, but this is our reading of Table 2, not the authors' claim ◐.
  - Reconciliation: capability predicts *one-shot improvement* but not *benefit from inherited state*.
- **Debate: does editing the harness or improver help at all?**
  - Flex-RSI: +2 to +40 in 6 of 7 pairs ✓, but with unmatched rounds.
  - SelfImprove-Bench: editable improver 1.326 vs fixed 1.207 (n = 1) ✓.
  - Against: Rethinking-Eval (evolution 67.4 below parallel sampling 72.3, round 1) and RSI Tax (a bounded-note baseline matches at 66–71% fewer tokens, round 1).
  - No benchmark builds a matched-compute "no-edit" arm into its protocol.
- **Contradiction: harness transfer across models.**
  - Evo-Bench: "highly transferable reasoning structures" ✓.
  - SEAGym: asymmetric transfer, mostly neutral or negative OOD ✓.
  - Flex-RSI: 2 of 4 hand-offs help ✓.
  - One Recipe Many Harnesses (round 1): edits encode model compensation.
  - Likely cause: Evo-Bench pre-selects harness-sensitive tasks.
- **Contradiction: the meaning of "RSI benchmark".** Most items called "RSI benchmarks" do not test whether an inherited change does anything:
  - Singularity-Bench, AI4AI-Bench, CompressionBench, RSIBench-Data and RSI-Index are single-shot (L1–L2).
  - Only RSI-Env and Flex-RSI let the updated system or improver run later rounds.
  - Even they show structural, not effective, recursion (Duan §1.7).
- **Debate: breadth vs depth of search.**
  - HarnessOpt: breadth correlates with gain, trace reading anti-correlates ✓.
  - SEAGym: batch size is non-monotone. Batch 20 is best, batch 40 gains little, and batch 80 (most evidence per update) loses 17 pp ✓.
  - Both point to an attention or context bottleneck in the improver rather than too little evidence.

### Open problems
1. **A swap-test benchmark.** Improver generation × fixed solver states, at matched compute, with ≥ 3 seeds. Auditing-the-Product Prop. 3 defines it; none of the roughly 40 benchmarks implements it.
2. **Matched-compute no-edit and placebo arms built into the protocol.** Needed to fix Flex-RSI's unequal rounds and RSI-Env's unequal hours. Include TEB-style seed-null bands.
3. **Seeds.** The single-run norm (Evo-Bench, RSIBench-Data, RSIGym, CompressionBench, Flex-RSI, SEAGym) makes most leaderboard gaps smaller than run-to-run variance. HarnessOpt's resolution bands (with two runs per configuration) are the only built-in remedy.
4. **Selection-regret and peak-retention metrics as first-class leaderboard columns** (78.26% end-below-peak; selected vs best candidate).
5. **Grader integrity under self-modification.** Breakwater covers single-shot tasks. Nothing tests graders against an improver that rewrites its own verification across rounds (Masked Erosion is harness-level only).
6. **Drift in the rules of improvement**, not only in tasks or harness. For example: feedback granularity changes (Flex-RSI shows binary vs scaled feedback matters), budget regimes change, or the evaluator is swapped mid-stream.
7. **Frame revision / stale objectives** (Chen §9.6): no benchmark scores whether a system *notices* that its objective is wrong.
8. **Benchmark-construction bias.** Sensitivity-selected tasks (Evo-Bench) and sources that collapse alone (SEAGym HLE-only, which drops to 0) mean benchmark choice can manufacture or erase "self-improvement".
9. **Long horizons.** Streams are 3–5 tasks (Continual AutoResearch), 2–4 blocks (continual learners) or 3 sessions (RSI-Forge). Infrathon shows rankings flip with horizon.
10. **Weights plus harness jointly, with an inheritance gate.** RSI-Env accepts on validity only. No benchmark asks whether a self-trained model is a *better improver* in the next round.

### Where it is heading (to mid-2027)
- **Consolidation into a few protocol standards.** Likely survivors:
  - HarnessOpt/VeRO-style trusted evaluators with resolution bands;
  - SEAGym-style multi-view records;
  - Breakwater-style hardened graders;
  - Auditing's claim-indexed reporting.

  Expect NeurIPS 2027 D&B reviewers to demand seeds, matched-compute baselines and held-out splits as table stakes.
- **The ICLR 2027 wave is decided around late Jan 2027.** Many of these benchmarks are under review there (RSI-Env, RSIBench-Data, PAST-Bench, GDPevo, AI4AI, EvoHarnessBench, Singularity-Bench, TEB, RSI-Forge, CLE, SkillFlow, Continual AutoResearch). Reviewer threads already push on scope and held-out validity (e.g. AgentSWE, RSI-Env responses).
- **From single-shot AI R&D to inherited multi-round.** Singularity-Bench and Infrathon will likely add multi-generation tracks. Flex-RSI already maintains a leaderboard.
- **Improvement-ability training data** (RSI-Dojo, RSI-Prime) creates contamination risk for the benchmarks themselves. Expect regenerable suites (GDPevo V2, SelfImprove-Bench generators) to gain value.
- **A "swap-test" or "process" benchmark is the predictable next entry** (high likelihood by mid-2027). The most probable source is the SJTU/Theseus group (SelfImprove-Bench + Duan survey) or the Auditing authors.

### Connection to our ideas
- **#2 Forced-Quota and #3 Gate, Not Willingness.**
  - SelfImprove-Bench is the direct motivation: 0 of 915 retained opinions touch the improver in main runs ✓, and a fixed vs editable improver differ by only 0.119 at n = 1 ✓ (the sign flips across backbones: Opus-editable scores 0.941, per FULLTEXT_VERIFICATION).
  - Flex-RSI forces improver self-edits every round (400-line cap) with no gate on them. That is a natural "always-forced" arm.
  - Neither measures the propose→propagate→pay-off funnel, so it is still open.
- **#4 Order-2 Audit and the swap test.**
  - Auditing-the-Product supplies the estimand and the 4/26 statistic. "Why Is RSI Hard to Verify?" supplies tests.
  - Our nested-replay design is exactly the missing benchmark item (Open Problem 1). Cite both and position the work as "the first matched-budget swap test, run".
- **#6 Meta-Overfitting.** The evidence on harness transfer across models is mixed and uncontrolled:
  - SEAGym's asymmetric cross-backend OOD ✓;
  - Flex-RSI's 2 of 4 hand-offs ✓;
  - SelfImprove-Bench's G3 directional asymmetry (Hero→Sweepmine positive, reverse negative) ✓.

  None wipes memory or grades domain distance, so the distance-dose design remains differentiated.
- **#7 Varying Goals / #9 MetaShift.**
  - EvoHarnessBench, the continual-learners study, Δτ-Bench, PACE-Bench and ServeLearnBench cover task-, harness- and environment-drift at the object level, so "another drift benchmark" is saturated.
  - Flex-RSI's binary-vs-scaled feedback finding ✓ is the closest evidence that changing the *rules of improving* matters. That supports MetaShift's framing.
- **#8 Openness Ladder.**
  - HarnessOpt's lever-breadth ρ ✓ and the continual learners' surface-size↔stability trade-off ✓ are the two strongest correlational anchors.
  - Both are confounded (breadth is an outcome; surface is tied to method), which is exactly what a randomized ladder fixes.
  - RSI-Env's three guidance settings are a coarse analogue on the *goal* axis.
- **#1 Taught, Not Selected.**
  - HarnessOpt's negative trace-reading correlation ✓ is a surprising counterpoint: optimizers barely read traces. The pilot should measure reading share.
  - RSI-Forge's shortcut codebook and Singularity-Bench's attack bank are ready-made sources of "environment errors".
- **#5 Order-0 Rewards Breed Routers.**
  - Evo-Bench's GPT-5.6 Sol case study shows the evolved harness is a domain router ("naive domain routing instead of… shared mechanisms") ✓. This is direct qualitative support.
  - Use Evo-Bench or HarnessOpt as an order-0 substrate and score order 1 on top.
- **Practical substrate choice for Dan (cheap, open, held-out).**
  - HarnessOpt-Bench protocol (resolution bands) plus SelfImprove-Bench generators (unlimited fresh instances, cheap games).
  - Avoid GPU-heavy gyms: Singularity-Bench, RSIGym, VibeTraining, RSI-Env.
  - Always report seed bands (TEB), selection regret (RSIBench-Data) and matched-compute no-edit arms (Flex-RSI's gap).

## Harness ↔ weights: co-evolution, distillation, Baldwin effects

*Marks: ✓ = checked in the full text, this session or in FULLTEXT_VERIFICATION.md, with section or table cited. ◐ = from an abstract only (arXiv, S2 or OpenReview). † = taken from earlier project notes and not re-checked. Full texts are cached under `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-nlp-lab-paper-search/b6ee0fee-4f54-593f-a9fa-6ec1fa49d4e7/scratchpad/papers/<id>/paper.txt`.*

**Read in full this session (method, results, limitations):**
- Harness-Zero, Harness Evolution Hits a Ceiling, CoEvo-RSI, HERD, JoMoHa, Harness Annealing
- CODA, Evo², SIA, WHALE, HarnessAdapt-RL, Harness-S
- Co-Harness, HELIX, Self-HPO (Tables 1–3), Knowledge-in-the-Harness (2611.15268)

**Read in part:** HASE, WeAct, SEAL, and the surveys 2607.13104 and 2609.11873 (the cited sections only).

**Fresh searches run:** 4 alphaXiv recency queries, 9 ICLR-2027 OpenReview queries, and S2 forward citations of 4 papers. Harness-Zero and CoEvo-RSI are not yet indexed by S2; WHALE has 20 citers. The adversarial fact-check added further OpenReview lookups to confirm the ICLR IDs of 8 papers.

### At a glance
- **What this corner is.** It covers four kinds of loop:
  - **Co-evolution:** a harness (prompts, tools, memory, middleware, control logic) and model weights are improved in one loop, either alternating or jointly.
  - **Distillation:** behaviour that the harness induces is moved into the weights so the harness can be removed.
  - **Improver weights:** the weights of the model that *writes* harnesses are trained (Evo²).
  - **Baldwin question:** does a supportive harness during training *help* the weights learn ("assist"), or does it *substitute for* learning ("hiding", i.e. harness dependence)?
- **Size.** As a *method* lane it is saturated:
  - about 25 arXiv method papers between Jul and Nov 2026;
  - more than 12 ICLR 2027 co-evolution submissions (round-2 sweep †);
  - 9 more ICLR 2027 harness-distillation or internalization submissions found this session ◐.
- **State of the art, by setting:**
  - **Distillation, single round.** Harness-Zero: Qwen3.5-9B with the specialized harness removed scores 44.3 macro-average. That beats the base model *with* the evolved harness (41.7) ✓ (Table 2).
  - **Joint RL.** JoMoHa reaches 97.0% on ALFWorld ✓.
  - **Multi-round.** CoEvo-RSI runs 10 rounds and averages over 3 runs ✓ (§4.1).
  - **Long-horizon continual learning.** HERD runs 25 stages × 3 seeds and deploys bare weights ✓.
- **Consensus 1: one-sided optimisation usually leaves gains on the table.** The joint method beats its one-sided arms in WHALE, JoMoHa, CoEvo-RSI and HarnessAdapt-RL ✓. Two caveats:
  - SIA has **no weight-only arm**. It compares only harness-only against harness+weights ✓ (Table 3).
  - In Self-HPO, the harness-only Meta-Harness baseline essentially ties the joint method on SWE-V (69.1±1.9 vs 69.5±0.9). The joint method leads only on the 3-benchmark average (63.5 vs 64.8) ✓ (Table 1).
  - No paper matches compute across arms.
- **Consensus 2: naive coupling breaks.**
  - Alternating updates can collapse: JoMoHa falls from 90.5 to 31.5 ✓.
  - Co-evolved pairs become mutually specialised (CODA ✓; CoEvo-RSI's "brain–body mismatch" ✓).
  - Plain SFT on trajectories collected under a supportive harness creates harness dependence (Harness Annealing ✓, TAME ◐, harness entanglement l8aeyLANkN ◐).
- **Emerging regularity, the Baldwin sign.** Support *assists* weight learning when three conditions hold: it is gated to cases where every rollout failed, it is expressed in the deployment action space, and it supervises decisions rather than answers. Support *hides* learning when it is always on or reveals the answer. One shared mechanism has been proposed: the share of GRPO groups with mixed outcomes. Evidence: HarnessAdapt-RL, Harness-S, teacher-free co-evolution and Harness-Zero Table 3 ✓.
- **Biggest open problem.** No multi-round loop has a compute-matched, multi-seed, per-round decomposition into harness effect, weight effect and their interaction, with a placebo. So we do not know whether harness↔weights loops *compound* or just front-load one round of gains. A second gap: no work trains the improver on a signal of successor quality. TAME's reward for transfer after the model update is the closest ◐.

### Taxonomy
The surveys split this corner on two axes.
- **What is updated.** θ = weights, Σ = scaffold (i.e. the harness). This comes from [2607.13104](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.13104) §3.2 ✓.
- **Distributional vs action-level self-reference.** This comes from the same section ✓.

Ren et al. list "Parametric Distillation and Joint Optimization" as a future direction because of its credit-assignment problem: should a failure be fixed by a prompt, a tool wrapper or a gradient update? ✓ (§9.2 "Future Directions", item 3; an earlier draft said §10).

The alphaXiv survey [2611.recursive-self-improvement-llm-agents](https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2611.recursive-self-improvement-llm-agents) is said to *exclude* executor-weight updates, which would put this corner outside its scope †. The link is not a valid arXiv ID and could not be re-opened.

Duan et al. [2609.11873](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11873) supply the test we need: "structural vs effective recursion". Does a revised mechanism persist, *and* does it yield stronger successors under comparable budgets and independent evaluation? ✓ (§1.7). No paper in this chapter meets the "effective" bar.

| Approach | Representative papers | What persists across rounds |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Alternating co-evolution with an external improver** (harness search ↔ SFT, RSFT or RL) | WHALE, Co-Harness, SIA, VACE, CoEvo-RSI, CoTrace, HELIX (data only), HarnessAdapt-RL, ModHarness-RL | harness and weights; the improver is frozen |
| **B. Self-referential co-evolution** (the policy writes its own harness, or one policy both acts and edits) | HASE, Self-HPO, Teacher-free 2611.15268, JoMoHa (trained Engineer), ACE-RL, MECA ◐, LEAH † (title only) | harness and weights; the improver is the policy or shares it |
| **C. Improver-weight training** (train the harness writer; the executor may stay frozen) | Evo² (executor frozen), MetaEvolve, TAME ◐ (rewarded on transfer after the update), JoMoHa's Engineer | improver weights and harness |
| **D. Harness → weights distillation or internalization** (remove the harness at deployment) | Harness-Zero, Ceiling (LoRA arms), HERD (every stage), Harness Annealing, Harness2Policy ◐, SkillCore ◐, Harness-Aware Distillation ◐, HPD †, Latent Harness ◐ (activations), EvoIn † | weights (plus a minimal harness) |
| **E. Skill/memory ↔ policy co-evolution** (the harness narrowed to a skill bank or memory) | SkillRL, ReSkill, ARISE and Evolving-RL (audited by CODA), SkillDuet, MDSKILL ◐, ENGRAM ◐, TrackRL ◐, SEAL (self-edits) | skill bank and weights |
| **F. Training under support: Baldwin assist vs hiding** | HarnessAdapt-RL, Harness-S, AutoScaffold ◐, Harness Annealing, TAME ◐, CODA, Multi-Harness RL, One-Policy-Many-Harnesses ◐, harness entanglement ◐, Harness Scaling ◐ | the question is what the weights keep once support is removed |
| **G. Lever choice and theory** | Ceiling (process vs content), Not All Experience †, Where Should Learning Live †, Policy-Is-a-Harness ◐, Where to Adapt at Test Time ◐ | rules for where an improvement should live |
| **H. Modular weights as harness-like actions** | WeAct (mentor), Differentiable Harness ◐ (KV cache), Latent Harness ◐ | the boundary blurs: adapters or caches become an editable "harness" |

### Paper cards

**Harness-Zero: Harness Distillation via Agent-as-Harness** ([2609.24974](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.24974), 21 Sep 2026; ICLR27 sub rZ7eO7DZmc ✓ ID resolves; PKU/Google/HKUST †)
- *What it does.* A harnessing agent reads a reference harness K, adapted from the evolved harness h⋆. It reviews each student proposal before execution and either passes it or replaces it with a minimal correction in the *target* harness's action space. The student is then SFT'd on these reviewed trajectories.
- *Setup.*
  - Student: Qwen3.5-9B. Harnessing agent: GPT-5.6 Sol. h⋆ evolved by Kimi K3.
  - Target harness: mini-SWE-agent with a single Bash tool.
  - Benchmarks: SpreadsheetBench Verified (100 test), AppWorld (168 test), USPTO (100 test).
  - Training: LoRA rank 32, 2 epochs, 487/282/500 rollouts, **seed 42 only**, single-run pass@1 ✓ (§4.1, App. E.3).
- *Key results.*
  - Macro-average under h rises from 23.3 to 44.3, vs 41.7 for the base model with h⋆ attached ✓ (Table 2).
  - USPTO: distilled 30.0 vs 38.0 with h⋆. Domain knowledge transfers less well than procedure ✓ (Obs. 3).
  - Ablation (USPTO only, Table 3 ✓):
    - SFT on the teacher's trajectories under h⋆ drops to 3.0 (action-space mismatch).
    - Plain teacher rollouts, and the student under h⋆, both leave the student at the 12.0 base.
    - Oracle-answer review reaches 98.6% collection success but only 15.0 on test.
    - K-guided review reaches 30.0.
  - 82.3% recovery across 28 harness-exclusive behaviours ✓ (Table 4).
  - At inference, agent-as-harness beats code-as-harness on frontier models, 81.1 vs 78.1 averaged over six benchmark–model settings ✓ (Table 1). The advantage turns negative with weaker reviewers: −12.0 on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B ✓ (App. F, Table 8).
- *Limitations and critiques.*
  - One seed; the ablation covers one domain.
  - Review costs 2.4× latency on USPTO ✓.
  - Our ICLR sweep notes it never compares against a frozen-harness RL baseline †.
  - It is the purest instance of "amplify-then-distill". It shows that naive distillation of amplified trajectories *fails*, and that it works only when supervision is re-expressed in the deployment action space.

**Harness Evolution Hits a Ceiling: When Weight Training Should Begin** ([2610.11655](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11655), 8 Oct 2026; ICLR27 sub FPaMYO47j4 ✓ ID resolves)
- *What it does.* Runs a self-evolving harness loop on DeepPlanning, then crosses seed vs evolved harness with base vs LoRA weights. Failures are labelled F1–F4: process failures (blocked calls, loops, exhausted budgets) vs content failures (a poor delivered plan).
- *Setup.*
  - Qwen3.5-4B and 9B, plus 7 other evolution lines (nine lines on eight models in total).
  - 48 dev and 72 held-out tasks; 4 rollouts per cell; anchors measured on the same night.
  - Transfer check: WebArena-Lite, 117 unseen tasks.
- *Key results.*
  - Held-out score: 4B 0.164 → 0.297, 9B 0.323 → 0.442 ✓ (Table 1).
  - LoRA trained on evolved-harness trajectories and run under the *seed* harness gains +0.126 (4B) and +0.131 (9B) held-out ✓.
  - On 4B the adapter stacks with the harness (+0.082). On 9B it substitutes for it (+0.007) ✓.
  - The answer-shuffled placebo falls 0.158 (dev) and 0.227 (held-out) below base, **9B only** ✓ (Table 10).
  - Full fine-tuning beats LoRA by +0.044 / +0.042 ✓.
  - The 9B adapter cuts F4 (content failures) from 28% to 5% held-out ✓.
  - WebArena-Lite: the harness gains +0.088. Adapters add nothing, because the gain lives in "what the model sees" ✓ (§7).
- *Limitations and critiques.*
  - The 4B ablation cells use 2 rollouts. There is no matched-budget test-time-search baseline, and a converter inflates scores by about 0.025 ✓ (Limitations).
  - Only one harness→weights round.
  - The authors say the ceiling belongs to the loop's evidence package, not to harness evolution in general ✓ (§6.2).

**CoEvo-RSI: When Harnesses Evolve, Which Models Should Follow?** ([2610.25078](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25078), 18 Oct 2026; NUS/A*STAR ✓)
- **ICLR link corrected.** An earlier draft linked ICLR27 sub 7UXKgr1Akp. That submission is titled "CoEvo-RSI: A Recursive Self-Improvement Framework for Long-Horizon Model–Harness Co-Evolution". Its abstract describes a different method: per-task scoring of each component, and 40 rounds on four benchmarks. So it is either a different paper with the same name or a substantially different version. Treat it as unlinked ◐.
- *What it does.* A meta-agent draws on a shared archive of harnesses, checkpoints and histories. Each round it develops a harness, selects or merges a checkpoint, and adapts the model by SFT on its own rejection-sampled trajectories. It introduces the Turn-level Interface Mismatch Rate (TIMR).
- *Setup.*
  - Qwen3.5-9B; meta-agent DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash in Codex.
  - 10 rounds, K=8 candidates; full-parameter SFT on 4×H100; averaged over 3 runs.
  - Tasks: Who&When, TraceElephant, RBAC Spider/BIRD, HomeBench ✓ (§4.1).
- *Key results.*
  - TraceElephant Who accuracy: 70.78 vs 56.62 for DeepSeek-V4-Pro ✓ (Table 1).
  - Who&When Algo: 62.17, *below* direct DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at 68.25 ✓.
  - Ablations on Who&When Algo, all single-benchmark ✓ (§4.3):
    - Harness-only has TIMR > 1% in 8/10 rounds;
    - Model-only reaches at most 35% SA;
    - Latest-only regresses at round 4 and ends lowest;
    - the full method reuses **round-4 weights at rounds 6 and 8**.
  - *Correction:* our round-1 note said "round-3 weights at round 10".
- *Limitations.* No compute-matched decomposition. Held-out tests are same-domain only. TIMR captures only interface violations (authors' caveat ✓).

**HERD: Harness-Evolving Recursive Distillation for Continual Learning** ([2610.31401](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31401), 22 Oct 2026; not found on ICLR27 †)
- *What it does.* At every stage of a task stream:
  - the harness evolves skills plus a bounded high-residual memory;
  - the frozen previous checkpoint, given privileged context (skill plus verified answer), teaches the student;
  - distillation is drift-constrained by two anchors, the previous checkpoint and base θ0.
  Only the weights are deployed.
- *Setup.* Qwen3.5-4B; TRACE+17 with 25 stages; 3 seeds; ablations on a single seed ✓ (Fig. 4).
- *Key results* (Table 1 ✓):
  - AA 0.706. Acquisition 0.713 vs 0.715 for Seq-LoRA (statistically tied).
  - Forgetting 0.010 vs 0.019–0.032 for the parametric baselines. ΔC −0.063 vs −0.200 to −0.240.
  - Context-only learners (ACE 0.427, HCL 0.433) barely beat base (0.419). The harness alone does almost nothing on this stream.
  - Without skills, acquisition drops 4.5 and AA drops 5.0 ✓ (Fig. 4). The harness's job is to choose *what* to distill.
  - Attaching the harness after distillation changes the metrics by ≤0.3 ✓.
  - Cost: 10,723 s total vs 10,463 s for Seq-LoRA; OPHSD needs 659,000 s ✓.
- *Limitations.* One model, one stream, known task boundaries, and verified answers are required ✓. The skill writer is fixed at θ0, so the writer does not co-evolve ✓ (§2.3).

**JoMoHa: Joint Model–Harness Optimization with RL** ([2611.11499](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11499), 8 Nov 2026; HKU/Salesforce ✓)
- *What it does.* Trains two agents jointly by RL: an Engineer that writes executable harness code and a Solver. They share the task reward but have separate critics, plus peer weighting, a schedule and value normalisation.
- *Setup.* Qwen3.5-9B-class actors; 144 rounds × 8 paired episodes; ALFWorld, WebShop, DBBench. Baselines other than WHALE are copied from Harness-R1 ✓ (§6).
- *Key results.*
  - Naive alternation on ALFWorld: 83.0 → 90.5 → 78.5 → 48.5 → 31.5 ✓ (Table 2).
  - Fixed-harness cross-evaluation decomposes the decline: −47.5 = −34.5 (Solver decline, measured with the harness removed: 82.5 → 48.0) + −13.0 (compatibility loss) ✓ (Eq. 2).
  - Joint training reaches 97.0, vs 90.5 for Frozen Engineer (best checkpoint 91.5), 89.5 for weight-only and 80.5 for harness-only ✓.
  - 3-environment average: 70.3 vs 63.1 for WHALE, which was run locally ✓ (Table 4).
- *Limitations.*
  - Single runs; no seeds; no compute matching against RL alone.
  - The collapse diagnosis comes from one alternating run.
  - The decomposition shows co-adaptation damages the *standalone Solver*. This is Baldwin hiding inside co-evolution.

**Harness Annealing: Learning to Act with Less External Control** ([2610.01235](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01235), 1 Oct 2026; ICLR27 sub HOk367J7I0 ✓ ID resolves; SJTU/Berkeley ✓)
- *What it does.* Defines "harness internalization": learning to take over specified control responsibilities once runtime support is withdrawn.
  - The nested harnesses are H1 tools ⊂ H2 +state ⊂ H3 +workflow ⊂ H4 +verification.
  - HAT combines decision-level ("Layered") supervision with a curriculum over teacher trajectories from progressively weaker harnesses.
- *Setup.* Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B; SWE-QA and SWE-QA-Pro; scores from a GPT-5.5 reference-based judge; LoRA rank 64; **single seed** ✓ (App. A, Limitations).
- *Key results.*
  - Direct SFT on H4 trajectories scores **16.51 under H1, vs 59.93 for the untrained base** ✓ (Table 4). Even Direct H1-trained reaches only 32.45.
  - Layered H4-trained reaches 71.99 under H1. The H2-targeted checkpoint reaches 77.00 ✓ (Table 3).
  - At 35B the gains are smaller (base 78.14 under H1) ✓.
- *Limitations.* No equal-budget controls. Direct and Layered are not matched for tokens. The judge-based metric is a caveat. Our round-2 sweep calls this the strongest owner of "harness dependence plus a fix" †.

**Evolving Together, Failing Apart: The Skill–Policy Co-evolution Trap (CODA)** ([2610.20845](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20845), 14 Oct 2026; ICLR27 sub ZIBdUe2hGK ✓ ID resolves; Alibaba/PolyU ✓)
- *What it does.* Argues that "cooperative acceptance" ties the policy to its bank: an edit is accepted if it helps the *current* policy. It audits 4 co-evolution methods under semantic rewrites (T1), incomplete skills (T2) and misleading skills (T3).
- *Setup.* SkillRL, ReSkill, Evolving-RL, ARISE; 6 method–benchmark settings.
- *Key results.*
  - Worst-case success is 4.9–12.6 points below peak, erasing 52–93% of the skill gain ✓ (Table 2).
  - The *meaning-preserving* rewrite is the worst case in 3/6 settings. Consistency is 77.5–87.0, vs a noise floor of 91.9–94.4 ✓.
  - In one setting, the co-evolved policy without its bank scores 57.6% (n=5 evaluations). A policy never trained with skills reaches 70.6%, the mean of its last five checkpoints ✓ (App.).
  - That pure-RL run is itself unstable: it peaks at 87.5, then falls to 53.1 ✓.
- *Limitations.* Diagnoses without fixing. Covers skills only, not harness code or model upgrades. The bands reflect evaluation noise, not training seeds ✓.

**Evo²: Evolving the Evolver through Weight–Harness Co-Evolution** ([2610.13025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13025), 9 Oct 2026; ICLR27 sub Ppb1YoSRol ✓ ID resolves; Google DeepMind/UIUC ✓)
- *What it does.* One policy plays two roles over a tree search with crossover: Proposer (writes harness edits) and Reflector (diagnoses edits). EvoTIDE trains *the evolver* with SFT plus interleaved GRPO on the outcomes of harness edits.
  - **The task executor stays frozen** ✓ (§3, §4.1: "the fixed task executor").
  - So this is improver-weights × harness co-evolution, not executor co-evolution.
- *Setup.* Qwen3.8-27B (FP8, greedy) as both executor and evolver; Polyglot, SWE-bench Verified, LiveCodeBench; memory tasks LoCoMo and LongMemEval.
- *Key results.*
  - Polyglot 82.1 vs 62.6 for GEA; SWE-V 48.3 vs 41.0 for HGM; LCB 58.0 vs 56.0 ✓ (Table 1).
  - Isolating weight evolution: Polyglot +16.3 (p=.001), SWE-V +5.0 (p=.086), LoCoMo +9.3 ✓ (Table 5).
  - Best transfer in 5/6 directions ✓ (Table 2).
- *Limitations and critiques.*
  - In the proprietary-model table, Evo² reports "the better result of its two top-ranked harnesses" while each baseline reports one. This is a selection asymmetry ✓ (§4.4).
  - The SWE-V gain is not significant.
  - The reward is order-0 (the child's gain), which bears on Dan's idea #5.

**SIA: Self Improving AI with Harness & Weight Updates** ([2605.27276](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27276), May 2026; Hexo Labs ✓)
- *What it does.* A Feedback-Agent iterates on the scaffold, then switches to LoRA weight updates once harness progress stalls.
- *Setup.* gpt-oss-120b, LoRA rank 32; LawBench (191-class), AlphaEvolve TriMul, MAGIC denoising.
- *Key results* (Table 3 ✓):
  - LawBench: 13.5 → 50.0 (harness only) → 70.1 (harness + weights).
  - TriMul: 0.105 → 0.120 → 1.475.
  - Denoising: 0.048 → 0.241 → 0.289.
- *Limitations.*
  - Updates are sequential, not interleaved.
  - No weight-only arm and no seeds. TriMul is evaluated at test time with no split.
  - §8 names "coupled co-evolutionary Goodhart" (two optimisers working against one verifier) but does not measure it ✓.

**WHALE: A Simple Recipe for Joint Harness–Weight Optimization** ([2609.00196](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.00196), 31 Aug 2026; ICLR27 sub Gu5Zol8WcQ ✓ ID resolves; KRAFTON/KAIST/Stanford ✓, with Finn)
- *What it does.* Alternates online rejection-sampling fine-tuning with Meta-Harness search, switching on a fixed or patience-based schedule.
- *Setup.* Qwen3.5-2B for SearchQA (7 sets) and AIME24/25; Qwen3.5-4B for Lichess puzzles; metric mean@8 ✓.
- *Key results* (Tables 2–3 ✓):
  - SearchQA: 48.34 vs 38.27 for weight-only and 38.29 for harness-only.
  - Math: 24.79 vs 15.42 and 0.42. Harness search helps math only after the weights move.
  - Stagewise: 43.02 on SearchQA. Adaptive WHALE: 52.82, with 23% fewer rollouts ✓ (§6.2.3).
- *Limitations.* Reports **"best test mean@8"**, i.e. the best point along the test curve ✓. No seeds reported in the parts read. JoMoHa's local re-run gets 80.5 on ALFWorld for WHALE ✓.

**HarnessAdapt-RL: Training the Whole Agent, Not Just the Model** ([2610.28069](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28069), 20 Oct 2026; ZJU ✓)
- *What it does.* During GRPO, two frozen teachers act:
  - one writes task-specific "mechanism-level" skills, which are removed at evaluation;
  - the other evolves tools and hooks, which are kept. A change is accepted if the pass rate or trainable rate improves without lowering the other.
- *Setup.* Qwen3.5-9B base; SWE-bench Verified, Multilingual and Pro; 3 evaluation repeats of **one training run per configuration** ✓.
- *Key results* (Table 1 ✓):
  - Average 44.9 vs 35.3 for GRPO and 39.0 for OpenHands-GRPO.
  - Near-answer hints during training, evaluated after removal: **32.7, below GRPO's 35.3**. Mechanism skills: 38.3.
  - Mixed-outcome group share: 46.5% with mechanism skills vs 39.0% with hints ✓.
  - Re-evolving tools as the policy changes beats freezing early versions (+2.2/+4.6/+2.0) ✓.
  - Swapping the evolved H2 back to H0 at deployment costs 4.8/7.7/4.7 points ✓ (§4.5).
- *Limitations.* SWE only, one model, no training seeds. The acceptance rule is not a significance test ✓ (Limitations).

**Harness-S: Learning from Sibling Harnesses** ([2611.04277](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04277), 3 Nov 2026; SJTU/Xiaohongshu ✓)
- *What it does.* Builds a fixed pool of sibling harnesses, which are invoked *only when all base-harness rollouts fail*. The same policy generates the rescue rollouts, which replace the failed GRPO group. The policy is then evaluated back under H0.
- *Setup.* Qwen3.5-4B/9B; AppWorld, SWE-Gym, DBBench; 3 independent randomized runs × 3 rollouts ✓ (Table 1).
- *Key results.*
  - 4B AppWorld Avg@3 under H0: 56.87 ±1.47, vs 48.98 for GRPO, 51.91 for H0-rescue and 46.69/47.84 for the always-on mixtures ✓.
  - 9B: 62.34 vs 53.31 ✓.
  - Effective-group rate: 79.38% vs 70.94% for H0-rescue and 64.69% for GRPO ✓ (Fig. 3).
- *Limitations.*
  - The sibling pool is fixed and built by a frontier harness editor (GLM-5.3) ✓ (App.).
  - The paper does not say whether "independent randomized runs" retrain the policy or only re-sample evaluation.

**Self-HPO: Self-Evolving Coding Agents via Harness–Policy Optimization** ([2610.22791](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22791), 16 Oct 2026; ICLR27 sub LxC7C6AMxv ✓ ID resolves; MSR)
- *What it does.* The policy analyses its own failures and proposes harnesses (H-step). It is then trained by RL under the chosen harness (P-step). Hard tasks seed the next search.
- *Setup.* Qwen3.5-35B-A3B; mini-SWE-agent seed harness; SWE-bench Verified plus Multilingual and Pro as OOD sets.
- *Key results.*
  - 2×2 cross-evaluation on SWE-V (Table 3 ✓): P0/H0 61.0; P0/H2 64.5; P2/H0 64.4; P2/H2 69.5.
  - The joint gain (8.5) exceeds the sum of the individual gains (6.9) by 1.6, a **superadditive** interaction.
  - Average resolve rate 57.8 → 64.8 ✓ (Table 1).
  - Harness-only Meta-Harness reaches 69.1±1.9 on SWE-V, statistically tied with Self-HPO's 69.5. The variant with an external proposer (HPO) reaches 71.6 ✓ (Tables 1–2).
- *Limitations.* One model family. The ± values look like evaluation spread, not training seeds †. One 2×2 at the end of the run, not per round.

**Knowledge in the Harness, Reliability in the Weights: Teacher-Free Co-Evolution** ([2611.15268](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15268), 11 Nov 2026; Brightendata ✓)
- *What it does.* The base model of a Gemma 4 12B agent diagnoses its own failed τ²-bench conversations and writes rules into skills. Each rule must pass code checks, counterexample self-review, a paired retest and a noise-calibrated gate. GRPO then trains a LoRA under the new rules.
- *Key results.*
  - After 2 rounds: +12.5 pass^1 in retail and +19.5 in airline ✓ (abstract in the PDF).
  - The 2×2 shows two things ✓:
    - rules carry policy *knowledge* that RL with the rules in context does not internalize;
    - weights make *already-solved* tasks reliable.
  - Rules can raise the RL signal ✓ (§5):
    - In airline round 1, the accepted update cut batch tasks never solved in four trials from 71 to 42.
    - In the other three runs the count changed by +6, 0 and +3 (Table 12).
    - So the effect appeared in 1 of 4 runs.
- *Limitations.* One model, two domains, 2 rounds. With 114/50 official tasks, single updates are mostly not significant ✓. Uses a DeepSeek user simulator instead of the leaderboard's ✓.

**Co-Harness (Meituan/AI2)** ([2607.22688](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22688), 17 Jul 2026; ICLR27 sub 53Ak0jvesg, titled "Co-Harness: Co-Evolving Harnesses and Models for Agent Post-Training" ◐)
- *What it does.* A HarnessCritic attributes failures and proposes validated local diffs. SFT on trajectories from the improved harness follows.
- *Key results.* Qwen3-8B/32B on AIME24/25 and HMMT25: average 58.5 (R0) → 73.5 (R1) → 78.9 (R2) ✓ (Table 6).
- *Critique.*
  - Only 2 rounds. No SFT-under-fixed-harness control, so the weight effect is not separated. Tiny test sets.
  - The 22-version case study runs on AIME24 itself ✓.
  - The ICLR version adds SWE-bench Verified/Pro and phrases the result more cautiously ("improves over two joint rounds") ◐.

**HELIX** ([2608.13951](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13951), 14 Aug 2026; HKU)
- *What it does.* A source-traceable harness substrate for "build–update–rebuild". It exposes 96 ports per product contract and 1,024 coupled recipes, or 4,096 when acceptance is selected independently.
- *Key results.*
  - +4.0% *relative* coverage over Pi on 100 AtCoder public-test tasks (Pi solves 50/100).
  - Exports 438 verified training records ✓.
- *Critique.* **No model update is run.** "Comparing held with rebuilt harnesses across rounds" is listed as a next step ✓ (§9–10).

**WeAct: Dynamic Weight Switching as Agent Actions** ([2610.26847](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26847), Oct 2026; CMU/Duke ✓, Yin co-first author ✓)
- *What it does.* Capability LoRAs (plan, search, write) over a frozen Qwen3-32B. Loading and offloading an adapter are actions in the tool-calling interface.
- *Key results.* WeAct-hard averages 45.47 across 8 deep-research benchmarks, vs 42.80 for Full SFT and 35.15–35.66 for merging baselines ✓ (Table 1). Also one code-adapter insertion and one writing refresh.
- *Critique.* The capability split is hand-defined. "Sustained continual learning … open" ✓ (Limitations).
- *Relevance.* It turns weights into a harness-like, editable library, a natural target for harness-style evolution.

**SEAL: Self-Adapting Language Models** ([2506.10943](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.10943), Jun 2025)
- *What it does.* RL on self-generated fine-tuning data ("self-edits"), rewarded by accuracy after the update.
- *Key results.*
  - Knowledge incorporation (Qwen2.5-7B): no-context SQuAD 33.5 → 47.0, vs 46.3 for GPT-4.1 synthetic data ✓.
  - ARC few-shot on Llama-3.2-1B: 72.5%, vs 20% for self-edits without RL and 0% for ICL ✓ (Table 1).
- *Critique.* Catastrophic forgetting under sequential self-edits, and an expensive TTT reward loop ✓ (§Limitations).

### Consensus, debates & contradictions
- **Consensus: both levers are needed, but each does different work.** The papers converge on a division of labour:
  - the harness handles process, knowledge and "what the model sees" (Ceiling, Teacher-free, Not All Experience †);
  - the weights handle content quality and consistency (Ceiling's 9B F4 cut, Teacher-free's "reliability in the weights", SIA's "domain intuition").
- **Contradiction: harness-only value varies enormously by task.**
  - Near-useless: HERD's context-only learners (0.43 vs 0.70 for weights); WHALE math (0.42); SIA TriMul (0.120 vs 1.475).
  - Large: Harness-Zero's h⋆ (+18.4); Ceiling 4B (+0.13); Self-HPO's Meta-Harness, which ties the joint method on SWE-V.
  - Only Ceiling's failure-composition rule predicts this *before* running, and only on one benchmark.
- **Debate: is distillation better than the amplifier?**
  - Yes in procedural domains: Harness-Zero's distilled 44.3 beats h⋆'s 41.7, and Ceiling's 9B adapter alone matches the evolution line.
  - No for knowledge: on USPTO, 30 < 38, and Ceiling's WebArena-Lite adapters add nothing.
  - How the data is built matters more than how good the teacher is:
    - SFT on the stronger teacher's trajectories under h⋆ *hurts* (3.0);
    - oracle review (98.6% collection success) gives only 15.0 on test.
- **Debate: Baldwin assist vs hiding.** The same type of intervention has opposite signs across papers.
  - *Hiding:*
    - HAT Direct SFT (16.51 vs 59.93 for base);
    - HarnessAdapt near-answer hints (32.7 < 35.3);
    - always-on mixtures in Harness-S (46.69 < 48.98);
    - CODA (57.6 without the bank vs 70.6);
    - JoMoHa (the Solver loses 34.5 with no harness);
    - TAME rank reversal ◐; harness entanglement −9.8 ◐.
  - *Assist:*
    - gated rescue (Harness-S +7.9);
    - mechanism skills (+3.0);
    - AutoScaffold (+7.2 ◐);
    - Layered HAT;
    - Self-HPO P2/H0 (+3.4);
    - Ceiling LoRA under the seed harness (+0.13);
    - Teacher-free rules shrinking never-solved tasks 71 → 42 (1 of 4 runs only).
  - *Proposed reconciliation:*
    - support helps when it *creates* within-group reward contrast on tasks where every rollout fails, and is expressed in actions the bare policy can take;
    - it hurts when it makes success trivial or acts outside the policy's action space.
    - Mixed-group statistics in three papers support this (HarnessAdapt-RL, Harness-S, Teacher-free), but **no paper varies support dose while holding everything else fixed**.
- **Contradiction: does co-evolution compound?**
  - Co-Harness claims "genuine compounding" over 2 rounds, with no control. Its ICLR abstract drops the word.
  - JoMoHa shows alternation collapses after round 1.
  - CoEvo-RSI's best checkpoints are *old* weights selected again.
  - WHALE shows small interleaved phases beat stagewise training.
  - Net: gains concentrate in early rounds, and inheritance or selection does the stabilising.
- **Superadditivity vs substitution.** Self-HPO finds harness × weights superadditive (+1.6). Ceiling finds stacking on 4B but substitution on 9B. The sign of the interaction likely depends on model strength; this has not been tested systematically.
- **Who writes the harness.**
  - External frontier writers dominate (WHALE, CoEvo-RSI, Harness-Zero, HarnessAdapt, Harness-S).
  - Same-model writers work with heavy gating (Teacher-free, Self-HPO, HASE). In Self-HPO, swapping the external proposer for the policy itself costs 2.1 points ✓ (Table 2).
  - Training the writer helps (JoMoHa +6.5 over Frozen Engineer; Evo² +16.3 on Polyglot), but the reward is order-0 (task score).

### Open problems
1. **A per-round, compute-matched decomposition of multi-round loops.**
   - For each round t, measure SR(θ_t, H_t), SR(θ_t, H_0), SR(θ_0, H_t) and SR(θ_0, H_0).
   - Add an answer-shuffled placebo and at least 3 seeds.
   - Use equal rollout and GPU budgets, and compare against weight-only RL and test-time search.
   - So far, JoMoHa does this once, on one run; Self-HPO once, at the end; Ceiling for one round.
2. **A dose-response for the Baldwin effect.**
   - Vary support strength and adaptivity during GRPO (none, gated rescue, always-on hints, a self-editing harness) with everything else fixed.
   - Measure what is retained after removal, with the mixed-group share as a mediator.
   - TAME and HAT already own the hiding diagnostic, so only the dose-response and the mechanism remain open.
3. **A prospective "which lever" predictor.** Ceiling's F1–F4 rule and the routing rule in Not All Experience are post hoc, on 1–2 benchmarks. Missing: a pre-registered predictor of harness gain vs weight gain across at least 5 domains.
4. **The writer should improve as the weights internalize.**
   - HERD's writer stays at θ0.
   - Evo² trains the writer but freezes the executor.
   - JoMoHa trains both but rewards only shared task success.
   - No one measures order-1 improvement: whether the co-evolved writer writes better harnesses for a *fresh* executor.
5. **Robustness of the delivered pair.**
   - Three kinds of drift matter: of the harness (CODA), of the model (upgrades), and of the deployment harness (entanglement, Policy-Is-a-Harness).
   - CODA-style audits should become standard.
   - Only two methods are trained for drift robustness: ARCHER (harness rendering) ◐ and TAME (reference harnesses) ◐.
6. **What is lost in distillation.**
   - Ren et al. warn that consolidation discards rare but crucial error-recovery strategies ✓ (§9.1).
   - Harness-Zero's per-pattern recovery ranges from 40% to 100%.
   - Whether safeguards and redundant checks survive distillation is unmeasured (Masked Erosion lattice † plus distillation).
7. **Selection hygiene.**
   - Weak practices are common:
     - reporting the "best test mean@8" (WHALE);
     - best-of-two harness selection (Evo²);
     - case studies run on the test split (Co-Harness);
     - acceptance rules that are not significance tests (HarnessAdapt).
   - Teacher-free shows that paired seeds do not pair dialogue outcomes (within-task correlation −0.09 to 0.07 ✓).
8. **Harness as weights.** WeAct adapters, Differentiable Harness caches and Latent Harness activation shifts are all "harness-like" parameters. Can harness-evolution machinery (gates, archives, crossover) operate on adapter libraries, and does it avoid co-evolution lock-in?

### Where it is heading (to mid-2027)
- **Method papers** will keep appearing, but reviewers will demand the controls listed in Open problems 1 and 7. Expect ICLR 2027 reviews of WHALE, CoEvo-RSI and Co-Harness to cite JoMoHa's collapse and CODA's fragility as required baselines (forecast).
- **The internalization lane will standardise on metrics.**
  - "Retained after support removal" (TAME, HAT) and per-behaviour recovery (Harness-Zero Table 4) will become the norm.
  - On-policy self-distillation with privileged harness context (HERD, SkillDuet, MDSKILL, ENGRAM) will become the default transfer tool.
- **Training the harness writer by RL** will become mainstream (JoMoHa, Evo², TAME, ACE-RL, MECA, likely LEAH). The debate will move to *what to reward*: task score, transfer after the update (TAME), or successor quality.
- **Gated rather than always-on support** in RL (Harness-S, Teacher-free, VACE) will become the default recipe. Baldwin-style analysis will be absorbed into "enrichment" theory (Understanding Enrichment 2610.02846 †).
- **Big labs are entering** (GDM's Evo², MSR's Self-HPO, Google's 2611.22299, Meta's PRD). This suggests production RL pipelines will co-train harness and weights, and academic leverage will shift to measurement, theory and robustness audits.

### Connection to our ideas
- **#5 Order-0 Rewards Breed Routers.** This idea sits directly in this corner.
  - Evo², MetaEvolve, JoMoHa's Engineer and ACE-RL all train improver weights on order-0 or child-gain rewards.
  - TAME's reward for transfer after the update ◐ is the closest thing to a successor-quality reward. It must be cited and differentiated.
  - Evo²'s Table 5 (+16.3, and +5.0 not significant) is a natural replication target for "does the trained evolver improve at order 1 on a fresh executor?"
- **#6 Meta-Overfitting.**
  - Evo² claims its evolved harnesses transfer in 5/6 directions, but all of them are coding tasks and the evolver was trained on them.
  - CoEvo-RSI admits its held-out tests are same-domain only.
  - A far-domain test of Evo²-style trained evolvers is a clean, cheap application of #6.
- **#1 Taught, Not Selected.**
  - Distillation propagates whatever rules the harness learned. HERD, Harness-Zero and Teacher-free all write rules from traces, then train the weights on them.
  - A misleading-trace channel would therefore become *parametric* after one distillation round.
  - Teacher-free's counterexample self-review and gate are the obvious defence to compare against.
- **#7 Varying Goals / #9 MetaShift.**
  - CODA (bank drift), Policy-Is-a-Harness (interface change) and CoEvo-RSI (old weights selected again) give motivation.
  - In a co-evolution loop, a "regime change" can come from the weights changing under a fixed harness. That is JoMoHa's −13.0 compatibility loss.
- **#2/#3 Forced Quota and Gate.** These belong in a gate taxonomy as concrete gate types:
  - VACE (17/44 harmful proposals ◐);
  - CoEvo-RSI's meta-agent selection;
  - Teacher-free's noise-calibrated gate;
  - HarnessAdapt's acceptance rule, which is not a significance test.
- **Parked: Baldwin hiding/assist (#18) and harness→weights compounding.**
  - Confirmed crowded. TAME, HAT, HarnessAdapt-RL, Harness-S and AutoScaffold together cover both signs.
  - The only defensible slice left is the controlled dose-response with mixed-group mediation (Open problem 2).
  - Multi-round compounding survives only as the measurement paper in Open problem 1.
- **Mentor link (WeAct).**
  - WeAct is the natural "harness made of weights": inserting and refreshing adapters are agent actions.
  - A gated, archive-based evolution of the adapter library could borrow CoEvo-RSI's checkpoint re-selection and CODA's drift audit.
  - This would connect Dan's improver-side ideas to Xunjian's own line without entering the saturated co-evolution method lane.

## Self-play, self-generated curricula & open-endedness

*Marks: ✓ means the number or claim was checked in full text. It was either re-checked in this fact-check pass on 2026-11-18/19 (see the Fact-check log) or read in full earlier this session. ◐ means abstract only, or a project deep-read from round 1/2 that I did not re-check. † means from memory or unverified. Local texts are in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-nlp-lab-paper-search/b6ee0fee-4f54-593f-a9fa-6ec1fa49d4e7/scratchpad/papers/<id>/paper.txt`. Flattened copies (`nf.txt`, `azr.txt`, `rz.txt`, `a0.txt`, `rf.txt`, `sp.txt`) are under the scratchpad. The placebo trial was read in full through alphaXiv fullText.*

**Read in full or in their substantive sections this session:**
- Method papers: Absolute Zero, R-Zero, Agent0, R-Few, SPICE, SPADE, Anchored Self-Play.
- Audit papers: Selection Is Not Learning; the zero-data placebo trial; 2611.06965 (abstract, §1 and §3.5).
- Survey 2611.08908, the full body.
- Survey 2608.10299, the full body.
- Survey 2607.07663: §4.4 and its failure-modes section.
- Survey 2609.11873: §3.4 and §6.
- Survey 2607.13104: the passages on self-play, games and self-generated tasks.

**Read at abstract or results level only:** MAE, OMNI-EPIC, False Frontiers, CompassPlay, Self-Play Pretraining, Training Stability, GenEnv, EnvFactory and CoEvolve. ActiveSaddler and R-Quest were read at the results or introduction level, with their key numbers re-checked in the text.

### At a glance
- **What this corner is.** Loops in which the system writes its own training material and learns from it. That material can be:
  - problems: proposer/challenger → solver;
  - opponents: zero-sum games;
  - whole executable environments: environment designer → agent;
  - or the order in which real tasks are seen: an adaptive curriculum over a pool.
- **How the surveys place it:**
  - Duan et al. (2609.11873) put it at **L3, "experience autonomy"**. The defining property is "learner-conditioned future experience acquisition". They ask that a task be *valid*, *at the right difficulty* and *durably beneficial*, and they note that "neither correctness nor estimated difficulty alone establishes learning value" (§3.4, §6 ✓).
  - Zong et al. (2608.10299) file it under **Stage 1, agent–agent** (adversarial) and **Stage 2, agent–environment** (co-evolution of tasks, feedback and interaction space) ✓.
- **State of the art, weight learners (verifiable domains).** Zero-data loops add about +3 to +10 average points on Qwen3-4B/8B-Base math or general suites:
  - AZR, R-Zero, SPICE, Agent0 ✓.
  - EvoHeir (2610.22029) adds an inheritance gate that keeps gains climbing for 10 rounds ✓.
  - SPADE moves from QA to **self-written Gym environments**: +8.1 over base and +5.3 over the best fixed-environment baseline at 30B ✓.
- **State of the art, frozen-weight (harness or memory) learners.** ActiveSaddler gets +4.4 pp on GAIA2 and +7.5 pp on TB2 over a fixed shuffled scenario order ✓. HERA and DAEDALUS show that self-generated or co-evolved tasks can stand in for curated ones ◐.
- **Consensus.**
  1. Pure closed loops plateau and then collapse within about 3–10 rounds. Causes include pseudo-label decay, invalid questions, and diversity collapse with length inflation.
  2. **External grounding** postpones this. Sources of grounding:
     - a corpus (SPICE);
     - a few human anchors (R-Few with 1–5%, Anchored Self-Play with as few as 50 references);
     - an executor (AZR);
     - a population or cross-fitting (PopuLoRA, CrossFit).
- **The 2026-H2 turn is audits, not methods.** Four papers:
  - "What Actually Evolves" (ICLR'27 submission) finds that gains are mostly *sharpening* of items the model already solves, and that later proposers teach no more than earlier ones ◐.
  - Selection Is Not Learning finds that 60 of 96 updates on verified tasks yield no gain ✓.
  - 2611.06965 finds that executor "grounding" bakes the generator's own false belief into the answer key ✓.
  - The placebo trial finds that, in code→math, correctness of the reward matters; format alone does not explain AZR's gain ✓.
- **Biggest open problem.** We cannot yet show that a self-generated curriculum **teaches what the learner cannot already do**, measured against out-of-loop ground truth at matched compute. Two related unknowns:
  - how much external grounding is enough (the "exchange rate", 2607.07663 ✓);
  - whether training the proposer adds anything over a strong fixed generator plus selection.
